# Weekly Paid Media Report

**Window:** last week = Sat 2026-10-24 → Fri 2026-10-30; prior week = Sat 2026-10-17 → Fri 2026-10-23.
**Data complete through:** 2026-10-30 (all three platforms). **Source for all figures:** ad platforms (google_ads, meta_ads, reddit_ads), via platform performance and window-comparison tools.

## Account summary — total spend

| | Last week (10/24–10/30) | Prior week (10/17–10/23) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Total spend (3 platforms)** | **$11,844.59** | **$9,892.11** | **+$1,952.48 (+19.7%)** |

The account's total spend rose **+19.7%** week-over-week, driven almost entirely by Google Ads (+$2,651.92), partially offset by Meta Ads (−$721.85). Conversions rose 33.3% account-wide (53 → 65) while blended CPA held ~flat at $182.07 vs $186.57 (−2.4%).

## Per-platform detail

| Platform | Metric | Last week | Prior week | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Google Ads** | Spend | $8,029.35 | $5,377.43 | **+$2,651.92 (+49.3%)** |
| | Conversions | 42 | 28 | +14 (+50.0%) |
| | CPA | $191.18 | $192.05 | −$0.87 (−0.5%, flat) |
| **Meta Ads** | Spend | $3,039.99 | $3,761.84 | **−$721.85 (−19.2%)** |
| | Conversions | 16 | 19 | −3 (−15.8%) |
| | CPA | $190.00 | $197.99 | −$7.99 (−4.0%) |
| **Reddit Ads** | Spend | $775.25 | $752.84 | **+$22.41 (+3.0%)** |
| | Conversions | 7 | 6 | +1 (+16.7%) |
| | CPA | $110.75 | $125.47 | −$14.72 (−11.7%) |

**What likely drove it** (daily spend shape, ad-platform reported):
- **Google Ads:** the +49.3% came from a weekday step-up — daily spend ran ~$833–$930 on the weekend, then held ~$1,200–$1,300 every weekday (Mon 10/26–Fri 10/30), vs a typical ~$550–$620 weekday pace two weeks earlier. Conversions scaled in line (+50.0%), so CPA was flat, not worse.
- **Meta Ads:** soft weekend days (~$320–$327) plus a lower weekday pace (~$450–$500 vs ~$555–$620 two weeks earlier) account for the −19.2%. CPA actually improved 4.0% despite fewer conversions.
- **Reddit Ads:** essentially flat (+3.0%) with a similar weekday-weighted daily pattern.

## Recommendations (one per platform)

1. **Google Ads — investigate before reacting.** A +49.3% spend jump with no campaign-level data to explain it is a question to investigate, not a fact to act on. The 10/26–10/30 step-up to ~$1,200–$1,300/day suggests a budget or bid change went live that Monday — please confirm what changed, since conversion volume kept CPA flat. (No change proposed.)
2. **Meta Ads — hold.** Spend down 19.2% but CPA improved 4.0% ($197.99 → $190.00). Nothing here warrants action; watch whether the lower weekday pace sustains.
3. **Reddit Ads — scale modestly.** Proposal `prop-487ea55d` submitted (status: **pending**, needs human approval): raise weekly budget $775.25 → $925.00 (+19.3%), on lowest-in-account CPA of $110.75. Caveat: 6–7 conversions/week is small volume — a one-conversion swing moves CPA by ~$18 — so this is a two-week test, not a full scale-up. **No change has been applied.**

## Caveats

- **Small conversion volumes:** Meta (16–19/wk) and especially Reddit (6–7/wk) make week-over-week conversion and CPA percentage changes noisy. Google's volumes are more robust.
- **Platform conversion definitions differ** (per each platform's data caveats); a "conversion" is not a qualified lead. Pipeline outcomes (leads, qualified leads, CPL) are a warehouse question and were **not** pulled for this report — figures above cannot be joined to pipeline without that separate source.
- **Campaign-level driver attribution was not possible:** `list_campaigns` returned names/goals only, with a fixture note and identical names across all three platforms — so spend shifts could not be tied to specific campaigns.
- Each platform's spend figures use that platform's own reporting; cross-platform "total" is the sum of the three, per the source-of-truth wiki.

All figures below are from the ad platforms via `compare_platform_windows` (CPA = weekly spend ÷ weekly conversions, both seen directly from tool output). Anchor date 2026-10-30 → last week = **Oct 24–30** (complete), prior week = Oct 17–23.

## Ranked by CPA change, last week vs prior week

| Rank | Platform | CPA prior week | CPA last week | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reddit | $125.47 | $110.75 | **−11.7%** |
| 2 | Meta | $197.99 | $190.00 | −4.0% |
| 3 | Google | $192.05 | $191.18 | −0.5% |

## What likely drove each

**Reddit (biggest improvement).** Conversions rose 6 → 7 (+16.7%) while spend rose only $752.84 → $775.25 (+3.0%) — the daily breakdown shows exactly 1 conversion every day Oct 24–30, so this looks like a broad-based efficiency lift rather than one lucky day. Main caveat: at 6–7 conversions/week, a single conversion moves CPA by roughly ±13%, so treat the −11.7% as directionally good, not precise.

**Meta (improved, but for the wrong reason).** Spend fell $3,761.84 → $3,039.99 (−19.2%) while conversions fell 19 → 16 (−15.8%). CPA improved only because spend was cut faster than conversions disappeared — this is underdelivery-driven efficiency, not genuine performance gain. If last week's spend cut was intentional, expect CPA to normalize if budgets are restored.

**Google (flat CPA while scaling — the healthiest signal).** Spend grew $5,377.43 → $8,029.35 (+49.3%) and conversions grew 28 → 42 (+50.0%). Holding CPA flat at ~$191 while scaling ~50% suggests added budget went into productive inventory, not rising auction prices.

## Caveats
- Windows are complete through Oct 30; no partial-week adjustment was needed.
- Reddit volume is tiny (7 conversions); platform conversion definitions differ from warehouse outcomes, and Reddit video campaigns may not join to the warehouse (per `get_platform_caveats`) — don't reconcile these CPAs against pipeline data.
- Meta's CPA gain should not be booked as an efficiency win given the spend decline.

**One recommendation:** Reddit's CPA ($110.75) is ~42% below Google/Meta (~$190) and its lift was consistent all week — a modest budget shift toward Reddit is worth testing, though its small volume can't absorb Google-level spend without CPA risk. Want me to submit that as a pending `propose_campaign_change` for human approval, or hold recommendations for the full weekly report?

## Conversions by Platform — Last Week vs. Prior Week

**Window:** tool-defined `last_week` vs. `prior_week`, relative to the data anchor date **2026-10-30**. **Source:** ad platform conversion counts via `get_metric_totals` and `compare_platform_windows` (platform-attributed conversions, not warehouse outcomes). The tools returned named windows, not calendar dates, so day ranges are stated relative to the anchor.

| Platform | Prior week | Last week | Change (WoW) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Google Ads | 28 | 42 | **+50.0%** |
| Meta Ads | 19 | 16 | **−15.8%** |
| Reddit Ads | 6 | 7 | **+16.7%** |
| **Total (all platforms)** | **53** | **65** | **+22.6%** |

**Read of the movement:**

- **Google Ads** drove the gain: +14 conversions week over week (28 → 42), up half again on already the largest volume. This is the platform to attribute the total-account improvement to.
- **Meta Ads** was the only decliner, −3 conversions (19 → 16, −15.8%).
- **Reddit Ads** ticked up +1 (6 → 7, +16.7%) — but at single-digit weekly volume, a one-conversion move is within noise; don't read a trend into it.

**Caveats:**

- Conversion counts are platform-attributed; the platforms' conversion definitions differ from warehouse outcome definitions, so these totals should not be reconciled 1:1 against pipeline data.
- Total-row percentages are computed from the tool-returned platform totals (53 → 65, +12); the +22.6% is simple arithmetic on those two tool-verified figures.
- Anchor date is 2026-10-30; any lag in platform conversion attribution (conversions reported on click date) means the most recent days can still revise upward.

Want me to extend this section with spend and CPA per platform (the full report format), or drill into what drove the Meta decline?

The proposal is submitted (prop-7ef3ac43, pending). Here is the completed report.

# Weekly Paid Media Report

**Reporting window:** last_week = 2026-10-24 → 2026-10-30; comparison week = 2026-10-17 → 2026-10-23. Data complete through **2026-10-30** (anchor date). All figures platform-reported (google_ads, meta_ads, reddit_ads) via reporting tools; window dates read from platform daily series.

## Account summary (sum of platform-reported figures)

| Metric | Prior week (10-17→10-23) | Last week (10-24→10-30) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $9,892.11 | $11,844.59 | +$1,952.48 |
| Conversions | 53 | 65 | +12 |
| Blended CPA | $186.64 | $182.22 | −$4.42 (−2.4%) |

## Per-platform detail

**Google Ads**

| Metric | Prior week | Last week | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $5,377.43 | $8,029.35 | +49.3% |
| Conversions | 28 | 42 | +50.0% |
| CPA | $192.05 | $191.18 | −0.5% (flat) |

Driver: daily spend stepped up from ~$833–930/day (Oct 24–25) to ~$1,203–1,303/day starting **Monday Oct 26** through Oct 30 — a level shift, not a gradual climb. Conversions scaled with it (4–5/day → 6–7/day), so the added spend held CPA flat.

**Meta Ads**

| Metric | Prior week | Last week | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $3,761.84 | $3,039.99 | −19.2% |
| Conversions | 19 | 16 | −15.8% |
| CPA | $197.99 | $190.00 | −4.0% |

Driver: spend came down faster than conversions, so efficiency improved modestly — but the platform shrank in volume. One week of this pattern isn't a trend.

**Reddit Ads**

| Metric | Prior week | Last week | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $752.84 | $775.25 | +3.0% |
| Conversions | 6 | 7 | +16.7% |
| CPA | $125.47 | $110.75 | −11.7% |

Driver: conversions rose on nearly flat spend. Best CPA in the account both weeks — but only 7 conversions, so the −11.7% CPA move sits within small-volume noise.

## Recommendations (one per platform)

1. **Google Ads — hold and validate before scaling.** Spend is up 49.3% week-over-week with CPA flat ($192.05 → $191.18). That's efficiency-neutral: the ~$1,200/day level is buying volume at the same unit cost. Confirm the Oct 26 step-up was intentional, and hold at this level until a second week confirms CPA holds — one flat week isn't evidence to push further. No change proposed.
2. **Meta Ads — do nothing this week.** Spend fell 19.2% while CPA improved 4.0% ($197.99 → $190.00); the two signals point in opposite directions (leaner but smaller). Acting on one week risks over-correcting; re-evaluate with next week's data. No change proposed.
3. **Reddit Ads — scale modestly (+20%).** Pending proposal **prop-7ef3ac43** (update_budget): raise Reddit weekly budget from $775.25 to ~$930. Rationale: lowest CPA in the account ($110.75 last week, −11.7% WoW) with conversions up 16.7% on +3.0% spend. **Status: pending human approval — not applied.** Given the small volume (7 conv/week), scale once and re-evaluate after one week.

## Caveats

- **Data completeness:** complete through 2026-10-30 for all three platforms (anchor date). The "prior week" daily series returned by the tool runs 2026-10-17 → 10-23.
- **Impression share unavailable:** `get_impression_share` returned a fixture stub in this deployment, so I could not verify whether Google's step-up was budget-cap release or auction-driven. Treat the driver as observed spend pattern, not verified cause.
- **Small volume warning:** Reddit's 7 conversions make its −11.7% CPA change high-uncertainty.
- **Source boundary:** conversions here are platform-reported; conversion definitions differ per platform and a platform conversion is not a qualified lead. Pipeline outcomes (CPL, qualified leads) live in the warehouse and were not joined in this report.
- All figures traceable to tool results in this conversation; the Reddit budget proposal is pending and nothing has been applied to any platform.

# Weekly Paid Media Report

**Window:** Mon 2026-10-19 → Sun 2026-10-25? No — the platform windows are calendar-anchored to the account's data anchor, **2026-10-30** (a Friday). The two windows the tools expose are:
- **"Prior week" = Sat 2026-10-17 → Fri 2026-10-23** (7 days, fully complete — verified against daily rows)
- **"Last week" = Sat 2026-10-24 → Fri 2026-10-30** (7 days, complete through 2026-10-30; this report was generated 2026-11-01, so Sun 10-31+ is simply not in the window, not missing from it)

**Data completeness:** all three platforms have spend rows for every date in both windows, and platform totals reconcile exactly to the daily rows (e.g. Google last week: $833.39 + $929.89 + $1,303.34 + $1,278.28 + $1,253.21 + $1,228.15 + $1,203.09 = $8,029.35). No partial days. All figures below are **platform-reported media metrics from the ad-platform tools** — no warehouse data was used, so pipeline outcomes (leads, qualified leads, pipeline $) are **not** in this report.

---

## Account summary (all 3 platforms, ad-platform data)

| Metric | Prior wk (10-17→23) | Last wk (10-24→30) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $9,892.11 | $11,844.59 | +$1,952.48 (+19.7%) |
| Conversions | 53 | 65 | +12 (+22.6%) |
| Blended CPA | $186.64 | $182.22 | −$4.42 (−2.4%) |

*(Cross-platform totals are arithmetic sums of platform-reported conversions; platform conversion definitions differ per platform, so the blended CPA is directional only.)*

---

## Per-platform detail

### Google Ads
| Metric | Prior wk | Last wk | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $5,377.43 | $8,029.35 | +$2,651.92 (+49.3%) |
| Conversions | 28 | 42 | +14 (+50.0%) |
| CPA | $192.05 | $191.18 | −$0.87 (−0.5%) |

**Driver:** spend scale-up that converted proportionally — daily spend jumped from a ~$820–890 weekday cadence to ~$1,200–1,300 starting Mon 10-26, while CPA stayed flat. This is a volume move, not an efficiency move.

### Meta Ads
| Metric | Prior wk | Last wk | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $3,761.84 | $3,039.99 | −$721.85 (−19.2%) |
| Conversions | 19 | 16 | −3 (−15.8%) |
| CPA | $197.99 | $190.00 | −$7.99 (−4.0%) |

**Driver:** an apparent budget cut — daily spend dropped from ~$595–620 weekdays to $320–500 — which shed 3 conversions at roughly neutral CPA. This is the only platform where the underlying cause is a spend decision, not a performance shift.

### Reddit Ads
| Metric | Prior wk | Last wk | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spend | $752.84 | $775.25 | +$22.41 (+3.0%) |
| Conversions | 6 | 7 | +1 (+16.7%) |
| CPA | $125.47 | $110.75 | −$14.72 (−11.7%) |

**Driver:** steady-state spend with slightly better yield. At 6–7 conversions/week this is a small base — one conversion moves the CPA double digits, so treat the improvement as directional.

---

## Recommendations

- **Google Ads** — No change. Spend rose 49.3% but so did conversions (+50.0%) at flat CPA; efficiency held. Keep the current level and re-check next week that CPA stays ≤$192 as the higher spend pace matures.
- **Meta Ads** — **Proposal submitted, pending approval** (`prop-b0411a7c`, status `pending`, never applied): restore weekly budget to ~$3,760 (the 10-17→23 level) from the current ~$3,040 run-rate, with a 7-day review and a rollback trigger if weekly CPA exceeds $198. Rationale: the cut shed 19% of spend for only a 4% CPA gain, and Meta's $190.00 CPA is now just below Google's $191.18, making it the cheapest incremental volume at the margin.
- **Reddit Ads** — No change this week. The CPA improvement is real but built on 7 conversions; hold spend flat and require a second consecutive week of sub-$125 CPA before proposing a scale-up.

---

## Caveats

1. **Window definitions are platform-anchored, not calendar-standard.** The "weeks" run Sat→Fri because the account anchor is 2026-10-30. Label them exactly as above when sharing; do not relabel them Mon–Sun weeks.
2. **Conversions are platform-reported.** Each platform defines its own conversion event; per the source-of-truth rules, these are **not** qualified leads and were not reconciled against warehouse pipeline data (no warehouse source was available in this session). The blended account CPA crosses those definitions and is directional only.
3. **Join limitation:** video campaigns ("Brand awareness video" runs on all three platforms) may not join to warehouse data (keyword-less), and platform conversion definitions differ from warehouse outcomes — so no platform-vs-pipeline reconciliation was attempted.
4. **Small volumes:** Reddit (6–7 conv/wk) and Meta (16–19/wk) — single-week percent changes carry wide uncertainty; that's why both recommendations require multi-week confirmation.
5. **Tooling note:** the `prior_week` daily-spend tool over-returned 30 days (Oct 1–30) instead of 7 for all platforms. This did not affect any figure above — every number was taken from either the platform totals or the correct 7-day slice, which reconciled exactly — but it means the daily charts for Oct 1–16 shown by that tool are outside this report's windows.
6. **Data is complete through 2026-10-30** on all three platforms. Nothing after that date existed in the windows used, and the week ending 2026-11-06 is not yet reportable.

Total Meta spend last week was **$3,039.99** (source: Meta Ads platform data, "last week" reporting window).

For context, that came on **$775.25 in spend**, implying an effective CPA of roughly **$110.75**. Want me to compare that week-over-week or against Google/Meta for the same window?

Google Ads spend (last 30 days, Oct 1–30, 2026, source: google_ads daily spend) has trended **flat for most of the month, then stepped up sharply in the last week**:

- **Oct 1–25:** steady rhythm — weekdays ~$750–$930/day, weekends dipping to ~$540–$570/day. Roughly $19.2k over those 25 days (~$765/day average).
- **Oct 26–30:** clear step change — daily spend jumped to ~$1,200–$1,300/day ($1,303 → $1,278 → $1,253 → $1,228 → $1,203), about **+45–50% vs. the prior weekday level** (~$830–860). The jump landed on Monday Oct 26 and held through Friday.
- **30-day total:** ~$25.4k (~$847/day average).

So the rough story: a stable, seasonally-patterned baseline for three weeks, then a sustained ~50% increase in the final five days — not a one-day spike. If that level was intentional (budget increase, seasonal push), fine; if not, it's worth checking what changed around Oct 25–26. Data runs through Oct 30, so yesterday is the latest complete day.

Short answer: I can't produce that number, and I don't want to fake it with the wrong source. Here's why, plus what I *can* give you.

**What I can't provide**
- **Pipeline value** is a warehouse metric. Per our source-of-truth rules, leads, opportunities, and pipeline $ live in the warehouse — my ad-platform tools only expose spend, conversions, and CPA, and none of them return pipeline data.
- **Per-ad breakdown** — my platform tools report at the campaign/account level; there's no ad-level performance view available, and no ad-level pipeline metric in any source I can access.
- I also won't substitute Meta's platform-reported conversions for pipeline. A platform conversion is not a qualified lead — mixing the two would misstate results.

**What Meta actually reported last week** (source: Meta ad platform, window 2026-10-24 → 2026-10-30, data complete through 2026-10-30):
- Spend: **$3,039.99**
- Platform-reported conversions: **16**
- Platform CPA: **$190.00**

**To get the number you want**
Pipeline value per ad requires two things I'd recommend pulling on the warehouse side:
1. Warehouse pipeline $ (with its own attribution) joined to Meta's ad/campaign identifiers via UTMs — and only if that join is clean.
2. Meta's ad-level identifiers in the query, since the platform side can't supply it.

If you can get me access to the warehouse (or a pipeline extract keyed by UTM/campaign/ad ID), I can build that breakdown. Otherwise, the closest verified statement is: Meta spent $3,039.99 and reported 16 conversions last week; pipeline value is unknowable from platform data alone.

Proposal submitted — **prop-87dee5d3, status: pending human approval.** Nothing has been applied.

**Proposed keywords — Google Ads campaign "Search - product terms" (goal: qualified_leads):**

1. `[product terms pricing]` — Exact match
2. `[product terms demo]` — Exact match
3. `"product terms software for teams"` — Phrase match

Match-type logic: exact for the two highest-intent commercial queries to keep query control tight; phrase for the mid-funnel comparison query to admit qualified variants without opening the floodgates.

**Why this campaign and why now** (source: ad platform data):
- "Search - product terms" is the account's only search campaign with a lead-gen goal; the other two Google campaigns (Brand awareness video, Community boost) have awareness/download goals and are not comparable for keyword expansion.
- Last 30 days (2026-10-01 → 2026-10-30, complete through 2026-10-30): spend $25,421.90, 131 conversions, CPA $194.06.
- Week-over-week CPA is flat: $192.05 (prior week) → $191.18 (last week), −0.5% — a stable base, not a one-week anomaly, which makes it the right place to scale keyword coverage.

**Caveats:**
- Keyword- and search-query-level reporting isn't available in this environment (fixture mode), so validate the exact strings against real query data before approving — and swap in the actual product nomenclature if "product terms" is a placeholder.
- Approval is required before any change takes effect; the proposal will remain pending until a human signs off.

## Monday synthesis — CPA by platform, last week (2026‑10‑24 → 2026‑10‑30, ad platform data, complete through 2026‑10‑30)

**Best CPA: Reddit Ads at $110.75** (7 conversions on $775.25 spend).

| Platform | Spend | Conversions | CPA |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reddit Ads | $775.25 | 7 | **$110.75** |
| Meta Ads | $3,039.99 | 16 | $190.00 |
| Google Ads | $8,029.35 | 42 | $191.18 |

**How it compares:**
- Reddit's CPA is **$80.43 (−42%) vs Google** ($191.18) and **$79.25 (−42%) vs Meta** ($190.00). Google and Meta are effectively tied.
- Context on scale: Reddit was only ~6.5% of total spend ($775.25 of $11,844.59) and ~11% of conversions (7 of 65) — Google drove ~68% of spend and ~65% of conversions.

**Caveats:**
- Reddit's 7 conversions is a very small volume — a single conversion swing changes its CPA by ~$14, so treat the gap as directional, not precise.
- Google's CPA is anchored by much higher volume; its absolute efficiency matters more to total blended cost ($191.18 × 42 conversions).
- One week only; I'd want a second week of Reddit data before reading the gap as a durable signal.

If you want, I can pull the prior week for the same three platforms to check whether Reddit's edge held week-over-week before anyone considers shifting budget toward it (any change would go out as a pending proposal for your approval).

Yes — the mix shifted meaningfully last week. **Google Ads gained share; Meta lost it.** All figures below are spend from the ad platforms, last week vs. prior week (windows relative to the data anchor date of 2026-10-30).

**Total spend:** $9,892.11 → $11,844.59 (+$1,952.48, +19.7%)

**Share of spend by platform:**

| Platform | Prior week | Last week | Change | Spend $ prior → last |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Google Ads | 54.4% ($5,377.43) | **67.8% ($8,029.35)** | **+13.5 pts** | +$2,651.92 (+49.3%) |
| Meta Ads | 38.0% ($3,761.84) | 25.7% ($3,039.99) | −12.3 pts | −$721.85 (−19.2%) |
